title: Open and closed source recollement on a vanishing topos
statement: Let $S$ be Noetherian, $f:X\to S$ of finite presentation and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion with closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$. Put $f_U=fj$ and $f_Z=fi$. For the induced maps $\bar j:V_{f_U}\to V_f$ and $\bar i:V_{f_Z}\to V_f$ of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles], the first is an open subtopos and the second its complementary closed subtopos. The functors $\bar j^*,\bar j_!,\bar i^*,\bar i_*$ on constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves are exact and preserve finite-stratification constructibility [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]. For every sheaf $F$ on $V_f$ the natural sequence $0\to\bar j_!\bar j^*F\to F\to\bar i_*\bar i^*F\to0$ is exact. These functors give the corresponding distinguished localization triangle on derived categories.

source.place: Section 9.3, printed pp. 22-23: the open/closed exact sequence used for the finite singular locus; the oriented product localizations are in Section 8.

proof.text: Put $P=V_f$, and let $u\hookrightarrow1$ be the sheaf represented by $U\hookrightarrow X$ on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Its inverse image $v=p_1^{-1}u$ is subterminal, since inverse image preserves finite limits [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. The projection formula in [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] identifies $v$ with the associated sheaf of the triple $(U\to S\leftarrow S)$. Apply [lem-trf-oriented-slice-localization] to this actual site object: it gives $P/v\simeq U_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}S_{\mathrm{Et}}=V_{f_U}$ over $P$. Thus [lem-trf-topos-complement-factorization] identifies the induced $\bar j$ with the open embedding of $v$.

By [lem-trf-etale-closed-complement-sets], $Z_{\mathrm{Et}}$ is the closed complement of $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$ in $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$: its sheaves of sets are precisely those terminal on $U$. Apply the factorization statement of [lem-trf-topos-complement-factorization] there and on $P$. For any Grothendieck topos $\mathcal H$, a morphism $h:\mathcal H\to P$ factors through the closed complement of $v$ exactly when $(p_1h)^{-1}u=0$. The same condition says that $a=p_1h$ factors through $i:Z_{\mathrm{Et}}\to X_{\mathrm{Et}}$, say $a\simeq ia_Z$. The oriented-product universal property [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] describes $h$ by $(a,b,t:b\Rightarrow fa)$. After this factorization it is exactly $(a_Z,b,t:b\Rightarrow fi a_Z)$, the datum for a morphism $\mathcal H\to V_{f_Z}$. The factorization includes all compatible $2$-morphisms and is natural in $\mathcal H$; applying these correspondences to the two universal triples gives mutually inverse maps, since their composites have the same projections and orientation as the identities. Hence $V_{f_Z}$ is the complementary closed subtopos, and its map is the induced $\bar i$. No closed subscheme is used as an object of $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$.

source.place: 08LY and its classifying property; etale-cohomology.tex 04CA(1); ILO XI 1.4.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-topos-complement-module-stalks] for $v\hookrightarrow1_P$ and the complementary embeddings of steps 1--2. This supplies $\bar j_!\dashv\bar j^*$ and $\bar i^*\dashv\bar i_*$, exactness of the inverse images, the restriction identities, and the actual stalk formulas for both extension functors. At $z=(x,t,c)$ the subterminal $z^{-1}v=x^{-1}u$ is $1$ exactly when $x$ factors through $U$, and is $0$ otherwise; the latter condition is factorization through $Z_{\mathrm{Et}}$ by step 2. The factor point is the same triple with its first point in $U$ or $Z$, since its projections and orientation are unchanged. For a short exact sequence on $V_{f_U}$, the stalks of its $\bar j_!$ image are therefore either the original exact sequence of stalks or the zero sequence. For a short exact sequence on $V_{f_Z}$ the same assertion holds for $\bar i_*$. Exactness of point inverse images and their conservativity [lem-trf-oriented-product-points-conservative] imply exactness of these image sequences: kernels and cokernels pull back to the computed kernels and cokernels, and an object with all zero stalks is zero. Thus all four functors are exact.

source.place: 03DI, 0710, 04EQ; sites.tex 08LY, 08M1; ILO XI 1.8 for point triples.

proof.text: For a module sheaf $F$ on $P$, take the counit $\varepsilon:\bar j_!\bar j^*F\to F$ and unit $\eta:F\to\bar i_*\bar i^*F$ supplied by [lem-trf-topos-complement-module-stalks]. At an open point their two-term sequence is $F_z\xrightarrow{1}F_z\to0$, and at a closed point it is $0\to F_z\xrightarrow{1}F_z$, including the specified adjunction maps. Their composite has zero stalks and is zero by conservativity [lem-trf-oriented-product-points-conservative] (apply it to the image sheaf); its kernel, image quotient and cokernel are also tested by exact stalks. This proves $0\to\bar j_!\bar j^*F\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}F\xrightarrow{\eta}\bar i_*\bar i^*F\to0$ is a natural short exact sequence.

source.place: 0710, 04EQ; the two stalk cases are the argument of etale-cohomology.tex 095L, now justified for P by the cited topos statements.

proof.text: We record explicitly the comparison needed for strata. The universal-property argument of steps 1--2 works with any second scheme $Y\to S$ in place of $S\to S$; none of that argument uses $Y=S$. For any morphism $q:P'\to P$ of such oriented products, let $j',i'$ be the inverse-image open/closed pair (defined by $q^{-1}v$), with induced $q_o,q_c$ on its two parts. The support description in [lem-trf-topos-complement-module-stalks] gives $q^*\bar i_*H\simeq i'_*q_c^*H$: the left hand side restricts to zero on the open, hence lies in the essential image of $i'_*$, and its closed restriction is $q_c^*\bar i^*\bar i_*H\simeq q_c^*H$. For the open extension, the adjunction map $j'_!q_o^*G\to q^*\bar j_!G$ is the identity on the open and has both closed restrictions zero, by the restriction identities. Its kernel and cokernel have both restrictions zero, because inverse images are exact. Such a sheaf is a closed direct image by the support description and is zero because its closed restriction is zero. Thus $q^*\bar j_!G\simeq j'_!q_o^*G$. These are canonical comparisons from the adjunctions. In particular on a stratum contained in $U$ either extension restricts as $G$ or zero, and on a stratum contained in $Z$ it restricts as zero or $H$, respectively.

source.place: 08LY closed support characterization; ILO XI 1.4 and 1.10(b). The comparisons are derived here from the support and restriction statements, not assumed base change theorems.

proof.text: The scheme $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since $f$ is of finite presentation and therefore of finite type. In particular $U,Z$ are constructible locally closed subsets of $X$. For a constructible $F$ on $P$, choose the finite partitions $X=\coprod X_\alpha$, $S=\coprod S_\beta$ in [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]. Use the actual scheme pullbacks $X_\alpha\times_XU$ and $X_\alpha\times_XZ$ as source strata, omitting empty ones, with the same $S_\beta$. Their composites are immersions, their images are disjoint locally closed sets, and they are constructible by the Boolean and Noetherian criteria of [def-weil-constructible-subset]. The restriction of $\bar j^*F$ or $\bar i^*F$ to each of these oriented strata is the inverse image of the original restriction to $(X_\alpha)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}(S_\beta)_{\mathrm{Et}}$; equality of the composite morphisms follows from [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Inverse image preserves a trivializing covering and constant finite module sheaves: it preserves terminal objects, epimorphic covers and the constant-sheaf functor by composition of geometric morphisms. Hence the new restrictions are locally constant with the same finite values, proving constructibility for both inverse images.

source.place: XI 1.4 for the stratum maps; finite-partition constructibility as in def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf; elementary refinement by U and Z.

proof.text: For a constructible $G$ on $V_{f_U}$ choose its source strata $U_\alpha$ and base strata $S_\beta$ from [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]. Regard the same immersions $U_\alpha\to U\to X$, together with $Z\to X$, as a partition of $X$. For a constructible $H$ on $V_{f_Z}$, use its source strata $Z_\gamma\to Z\to X$ together with $U\to X$, and its given base partition. These are finite constructible locally closed partitions: $X$ is Noetherian as in step 6, and locally closed immersions into an open or closed subscheme are locally closed in $X$ [def-weil-constructible-subset]. By the comparisons proved in step 5, the restrictions of $\bar j_!G$ to $U_\alpha\overleftarrow\times_SS_\beta$ are exactly the given locally constant finite restrictions of $G$, and its restrictions to $Z\overleftarrow\times_SS_\beta$ are zero. Likewise $\bar i_*H$ restricts as $H$ on $Z_\gamma\overleftarrow\times_SS_\beta$ and as zero on $U\overleftarrow\times_SS_\beta$. Zero is constant with finite value the zero module. This proves preservation of constructibility for both extension functors.

source.place: XI 1.4 for the stratum maps; constructibility follows by the explicit compatible partitions and step 5.

proof.text: Apply the natural short exact sequence of step 4 degreewise to a cochain complex $K$ of module sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], the four exact functors of step 3 act termwise on derived categories, and their termwise maps descend to them. Then [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] gives the natural distinguished triangle $\bar j_!\bar j^*K\to K\to\bar i_*\bar i^*K\to(\bar j_!\bar j^*K)[1]$, with the counit and unit maps already specified. It holds without a boundedness assumption, and in particular restricts to any bounded constructible categories using steps 6--7 and exactness.

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor; exact-functor factorization gives the termwise derived operations.

proof_origin.place: XI 1.4 and 1.10(b) for open slices and universal triples; closed complement proved by factorization using Stacks 08LY and 04CA(1); module stalk argument and constructibility refinement written here; derived triangle 0152.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q42-8593d1a44 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the three new nodes, every cited node's statement and the sources. Stacks etale-cohomology 04CA(1) is the sheaves-of-sets clause with left inverse, and it matches lem-trf-etale-closed-complement-sets exactly. Stacks sites.tex 08LW, 08LY, 08LZ, 08M0 and 08M1 support the open/closed factorization node. ILO XI 1.10(b) (slice at the object X'->S'<-Y') is the source of lem-trf-oriented-slice-localization, which step 1 uses with U->S<-S. Orgogozo is not in literature/: it is recorded as WANTED and proof_origin is agent. The factorization node is true: a morphism factors through the closed complement iff a^{-1}u=0, and through the open slice iff a^{-1}u=1; edge cases u=0, u=1 and a degenerate H all hold. The module-stalks node: I checked exact inverse images, j_! left adjoint to j^*, closed essential image {j^*F=0}, k^*j_!=0 (through free modules and strict initial objects), points with p^{-1}u equal to 1 or 0, the four point formulas, and that the unit and counit are identities; u=0, u=1 and Lambda=0 hold. Step 2's closed-source identification by 2-Yoneda on the universal triple is sound and never uses Z as an etale object. Steps 3-4 (exactness and the short exact sequence through exact points and conservativity) are correct. Step 5, marked elementary, is a correct few-line consequence of the support and restriction identities. In steps 6-7 the refined partitions are admissible, since def-constructible-stratification has no closure condition and X is Noetherian. Step 8 matches the hypotheses of the Mathlib leaves. There are no duplicates: lem-kun-04ca has the abelian clause only, lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-restriction is a base-factor statement, and lem-sp-ringed-topos-binary-descent is Mayer-Vietoris. No new node restates a clause of the item. No SGA is cited, the statement is unchanged, no target or unit is touched, and tool_uses is empty with only Mathlib leaves off-unit. One minor imprecision, not fixed: step 7 attributes 'locally closed in an open or closed subscheme is locally closed in X' to def-weil-constructible-subset, but this is elementary topology. No fixes.
